clue.text: When almost grown-up, a politician is flattering

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A rising young politician is busy buttering people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ADULT to ADUL; then A as written and TORY, a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawning, sycophantic praise is both adulatory and flattering: synonyms.

clue.text: Scientist making lots of noise about nasty war

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a din is a great noise, so making lots of noise suggests din

indicators.note: nasty signals the word war is to be roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A researcher protests loudly against a cruel conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making lots of noise' is an odd phrase for a noun, but a din is exactly that; 'about' is the container signal, not a vague 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the naturalist behind the theory of evolution, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Story associated with the German songs

parts.note: a story can mean a fib or untruth, a lie
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A tale linked with traditional German music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those of Schubert, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Sailor with coat goes over the road

parts.note: tar is an old slang word for a seaman
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: A seaman in his overcoat crosses the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over the' links: the road surface is metonymy for the road itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the asphalt surfacing used on highways, so it stands for the paved street by metonymy.

clue.text: One attuned to the heavens, I adore moon, star, possibly, right?

indicators.note: possibly says the preceding letters may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A stargazer confesses a love of the moon and stars, seeking agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I ADORE MOON STAR into RADIOASTRONOME; R for 'right' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies celestial radio signals is literally tuned in to the sky.

clue.text: Wire that you may well be holding!

definitions.text: Wire that you may well be holding!

parts.words: Wire that you may well be holding!
parts.note: a wire is an old word for a telegram, and also the name of the newspaper in the solver's hands

explanation.surface: A remark about a message or cable the reader is clutching.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraph sends wires, and the Daily Telegraph is the paper carrying this puzzle.

clue.text: Heather, about 10, is initially attentive

indicators.note: about means the plant word wraps around the remaining pieces

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: initially says the little word is goes in front of the number

parts.note: the figure 10 is ten

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old picking heather is paying close attention at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the common name for heather. 'initially' is not taking a first letter here: it orders the pieces, putting the little word before the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attentive is paying heed with their ears, adjective and participle both describing alertness.

clue.text: A final message worthy champion's spoken

indicators.note: spoken means we hear the words rather than read their spelling

parts.note: a worthy champion is a good knight, a valiant warrior

explanation.surface: A last word from a noble defender, delivered out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'); a good knight sounds the same as the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The farewell said at bedtime is the last thing exchanged before sleep.

clue.text: Sheep seen in summer in Oxfordshire

indicators.note: seen in says the answer appears within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A flock grazing in the Oxfordshire countryside in summertime.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across summER IN Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: A scheme to encourage worldwide traffic?

definitions.text: A scheme to encourage worldwide traffic?

parts.words: A scheme to encourage worldwide traffic?
parts.note: traffic here is commerce rather than cars, so the scheme is an unrestricted international trading system

explanation.surface: A plan to get vehicles moving around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce between nations without tariffs or quotas is the policy described.

clue.text: Fellow by the waves in a deckchair maybe

indicators.note: by means the man's name sits beside the water, after it

parts.note: the waves stands for the sea
Ted is a typical man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man lounges beside the sea in a deckchair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in a deckchair, one is sitting down, an example of the state.

clue.text: Blair tore around as one who would destroy oppression

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved round into a different order

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister rushes about posing as a freedom fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the nine letters of BLAIR TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberator frees people from tyranny, ending their subjugation.

clue.text: British engineer left to go to one foreign land

indicators.note: to go to tells us the first letter named is exchanged for the second

parts.note: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian British engineer
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Victorian engineer departs for a single overseas destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' swaps BRUNEL's L for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a sultanate on Borneo, a country abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Going the wrong way, naturally, with two females rather than one

indicators.note: rather than tells us the doubled letters replace the single one

parts.note: of course means naturally, as might be expected
one here is one female, F
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Someone going astray, naturally, with a pair of women instead of one.
explanation.walkthrough: In OF COURSE, 'rather than' replaces one F with FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or plan off course has strayed from its intended route.

clue.text: Getting ill again? Could be prepared for angels — rip!

indicators.note: could be prepared hints the letters can be made up into something new

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm over a sickness returning while angels tear things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be prepared' rearranges ANGELS and RIP; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who falls back into sickness after improving is suffering a recurrence.

clue.text: Cricket team from the central home counties area, not the full eleven

parts.note: central means in the middle
the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE

indicators.note: not the full means the last letter is dropped from the number

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and the usual term for a cricket side

explanation.surface: A county cricket side from the Home Counties fielding fewer than eleven men.
explanation.walkthrough: MIDDLESEX is a county cricket club based at Lord's; the Home Counties surround London. 'not the full' cuts XI to X.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlesex is one of the first-class county sides of English cricket.

clue.text: Fool getting inferior degree, not first

indicators.note: not first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a pass is a British university degree below honours level

explanation.surface: A dunce scrapes a low grade at university.
explanation.walkthrough: A pass degree is the British ordinary degree without honours; 'not first' drops P.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is an idiot, a crude synonym for a silly person.

clue.text: Get old attendant to drop off piano

indicators.note: to drop off means the musical letter is taken away

parts.note: a page is a young attendant, as at a wedding
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: An elderly servant is told to deliver a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older over time.

clue.text: Novel got rid of, not finished

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is dropped; the letters also sitting inside the word finished is a coincidence

parts.note: shed means got rid of, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Someone discards a book they never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard wrote a famous Victorian adventure book with this title.

clue.text: Experiencing hardship and walking along uncomfortably?

explanation.surface: Someone struggling for money also hobbles in tight shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: tight footwear pinches as you walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suffering from lack of money; read literally, it is a walker with sore feet from tight shoes.

clue.text: In this place without leader before

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: in this place means here

explanation.surface: A leaderless group was present at an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is an old poetic preposition for prior to.

clue.text: Man offering praise in church

indicators.note: in means the praise word sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A man singing hymns of praise in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude is a male first name, a specific example of a man.

clue.text: Ring of light held by army man as an expression of peace

indicators.note: held by means the ring sits inside the army letters

parts.note: SM is sergeant major, an army rank
a halo is a ring of light round a saint's head

explanation.surface: A soldier carries a glowing ring as a symbol of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalom is the Hebrew greeting meaning peace.

clue.text: Spike, I look anaemic!

explanation.surface: Someone cries out after being stabbed and going white.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as I'M PALE, how an anaemic person might describe themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike something is to pierce it on a point; and a person looking anaemic would say they look washed-out.

clue.text: Left-winger to arrive, blocking in motorway

indicators.note: blocking in means the arrival word hems in the road

parts.note: to come is to arrive
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A socialist turns up and causes a jam on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, read as letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A commie is slang for a communist, someone on the political left.

clue.text: Mono hit ed played was a hit for Glenn miller

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An old mono recording edited and played was a big band hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges MONO HIT ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller's 1939 swing record became one of the band's best-known tunes.

clue.text: The French going round street in old city of northern Ireland

indicators.note: in means the combined pieces sit inside the ancient city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: going round means the article encircles the street abbreviation

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: French visitors tour the streets of an old northern Irish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia; Ulster is often used loosely for Northern Ireland, though the historic province is larger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the historic northern province of Ireland, used loosely for the north of the island.

clue.text: Types of weapon that may be hidden in short sleeves?

definitions.text: that may be hidden in short sleeves?

explanation.surface: Weapons concealed up somebody's sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: Short sleeves cover only short limbs: the second reading is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are firearms carried by hand; and literally, tiny limbs would fit inside little sleeves.

clue.text: Entertainer who got everyone at home in stitches?

definitions.text: who got everyone at home in stitches?

explanation.surface: A comic performer had the whole household laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Singer company made household sewing machines; 'in stitches' means laughing or sewn.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is a performer; and Isaac Singer's sewing machines put stitches into homes everywhere.

clue.text: Musician offering last item in concert, strange man

indicators.note: last item in means take the final letter of the word

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
Peter is a man's name

explanation.surface: A performer providing the closing number at a concert is an odd fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter plays a brass instrument, an example of a musician.
